newsitem.title: UK: UK student loans sale to raise 3.1 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK student loans sale to raise 3.1 bln stg.

text.p: The British government's sale of student loan debt to the private sector could raise 1.6 billion stg ($2.7 billion) by the end of 1997 and 1.5 billion stg next year, an advisor to the government said on Friday.

"The sales (of student loans) are necessary to meet the government's manifesto commitment to keep within already announced spending plans for this year and next," Charles Keay, executive director at N M Rothschild told Reuters.
"Those plans assume sale receipts of 1.6 billion stg this year, and 1.5 billion stg next," he said.
Rothschild is advising the government on the sale of its student loan portfolio.
The Labour government said on Thursday it would go ahead with plans drawn up by the previous Conservative administration to sell the loans.

Twenty financial institutions have pre-qualified for the sale, allowing them to bid for the loan portfolio, and these institutions will receive a preliminary information memorandum within the next month, Keay said.
Once they receive this, they can bid for the transaction and a shortlist of contenders to buy the portfolio will then be drawn up.

Britain has transferred a host of public assets into private hands, including homes owned by the Ministry of Defense and housing loans made by local authorities, as part of its Private Finance Initiative.

Consortia of banks have bought these assets, and issued bonds securitised by their cashflows to finance the deals. Such a securitisation is also an option for the buyers of the student loan portfolio.
"The government is committed to the development of a wide range of public/private partnerships which transfer risk to the private sector," Keay said. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
